proposal.title: GCP pull request review assistant (first sketch)
proposal.body: Scope: review a synthetic pull request from an existing repository. The system reads the authorised diff and changed files with read-only access, Gemini analyses them, a guard checks the output, and draft comments are linked to changed lines. Assumptions: the repository host and its webhook already exist. The token is read-only and kept in Secret Manager. The region is to be selected. No repository code is executed, pushed or merged. Posting comments to the host is still an open decision. There is no native Terraform generator for this workload, so engineering is required. Nothing has been deployed or verified.

data.label: Existing code repository
data.description: Existing repository host, preserved unchanged. It sends pull request webhooks and serves the diff and changed files to a read-only token.

data.label: Webhook receiver
data.description: Checks the webhook signature, accepts only allowed repositories and events, and queues a review job. It does no analysis itself.

data.label: Review job queue
data.description: Separates intake from processing. Retries jobs, and a dead-letter topic catches failed ones.

data.label: Review worker
data.description: Reads only the authorised diff and relevant changed files through the read-only API. It never clones, builds or executes repository code. It treats repository content as untrusted data, calls Gemini, and maps findings to changed lines.

data.label: Read-only repository token
data.description: Holds the read-only repository credential, readable only by the worker's service account. No secret values appear in this diagram.

data.label: Gemini model
data.description: Analyses the diff. Model choice, regional availability and quota are not verified. Local tests use scripted replies.

data.label: Comment guard
data.description: Part of the worker deployment. It rejects comments that point outside changed lines, any proposed actions such as push, merge or run, and leaked secrets.

data.label: Draft review comments
data.description: Stores draft comments keyed by pull request, commit and file line, with a status for each job. Whether they get posted is an open decision.

data.label: Logs and audit
data.description: Records jobs, model calls, guard rejections and failures without storing source code in logs.

requirementDrafts.rationale: This prevents supply-chain or prompt-injection attacks from changing the repository or running untrusted code.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: 'Never push, merge or execute repository code.'
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: the system only reads the authorised diff and changed files. It never pushes, merges, clones to execute, or runs repository code.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Comments that point at the wrong place confuse reviewers and cannot be posted.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: 'draft review comments linked to changed lines'
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: every draft comment refers to a file and line changed in the reviewed commit. Any other comments are rejected.

response.message: The emulation has no failed checks: the design held together, with every flow connected and no rule violations. It's marked "blocked" for a different reason. None of the 8 components has a supported Google Cloud implementation in the generator yet, and the existing repository still needs a plan for how we connect to it without changing it. No change to the diagram will fix this. It's product engineering work: the generator needs native implementations for Cloud Run, Pub/Sub, Secret Manager, Vertex AI and Firestore, plus a read-only repository connection. This run on artifact fb97bef8… is the test case to reproduce the gap, and I won't shrink the design to make the check pass. So we can plan that work, which repository host should we build the read-only connection for first: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or something else?
